newsitem.title: USA: Glickman-EEP funding shows US will "go to the mat".
newsitem.headline: Glickman-EEP funding shows US will "go to the mat".

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said the Clinton administration's FY98 budget proposal for $500 million for the Export Enhancement Program showed the U.S. was willing to "go to the mat" to protect its farmers.
Glickman said the administration had requested the maximum amount of funding allowed under law. Funding for the EEP program has been capped at $100 million this year by Congress.

"That sends a clear signal to our trading partners that the U.S. is serious and fully capable of going to the mat for our producers if its necessary to challenge unfair trade practices and if market conditions require it," Glickman told a budget briefing.
"This is not meant to say that it is imminent that we're going to use it again but it ought to be in our budget at this level. We think the potential for using it is there," he said.
